title: Can't See the Forest for the Trees

mapping.sentence: An AI improved the author’s sentences, and quietly weakened what he was trying to say.
mapping.cue: Show the author's sharp original sentence become smoother while its question fades.

mapping.sentence: That experience opens Can't See the Forest for the Trees, a book about systems that miss the damage they cause.
mapping.cue: Keep the author beside both versions so the manuscript remains a lived experience.

mapping.sentence: The sentences sounded reasonable while doubt, urgency, and responsibility became easier to overlook.
mapping.cue: Restore three short margin marks for doubt, urgency and responsibility beside the smoother passage.

mapping.sentence: The book follows a similar pattern in companies, research, politics, and the technologies connecting them.
mapping.cue: Carry the same loss from a manuscript to a planning document, without claiming identical systems.

mapping.sentence: Each specialist can tend a necessary part while the consequences of the whole escape attention.
mapping.cue: Let separate specialists mark their own sections while the connecting consequence remains unowned.

mapping.sentence: The author remains uncertain, but keeps asking where people can still make a useful difference.
mapping.cue: Show the author keep an unanswered intervention question in the plan rather than closing it.

mapping.sentence: A smoother explanation can make a real conflict harder to notice, and harder to name.
mapping.cue: Hold the polished explanation beside the real conflict it made harder to name.

mapping.sentence: Begin with the edited manuscript, and ask what became less true when everything sounded more reasonable.
mapping.cue: End on both manuscript versions open for comparison.

defects.what: The translucent 'All systems align.' sheet sits on top of the operator and resident: its three grey text lines run straight across both faces (eyes/brows), the figures are washed out behind it, and the sheet has a tan outline frame with a wavy bottom edge (a framed panel over characters). Text lines through faces violate label/silhouette separation; the conflict being hidden reads as a rendering glitch rather than as concealment.
defects.fix: Make the polished explanation an opaque, unframed card that covers the pair completely (or slides in front of their bodies with its text lines kept above their heads), then lift/slide it away; never let text strokes cross faces. Drop the outline stroke.

defects.what: The 'real conflict' is never acted out. The operator and resident stand side by side facing the viewer with arms down and no mutual gaze; at the sentence-2 midpoint both wear mild smiles. The sentence is about something that became 'less true' and has an inviting-challenge cue, but no tension is visible.
defects.fix: Turn the pair toward each other, with contrasting worried and angry faces and explaining/recoil hands held through sentence 2, so the uncovered disagreement stays readable when the narrator says to ask what became less true.

defects.what: 'Begin with the edited manuscript': the magnifier floats in empty space above the operator's head on the right (and drifts further right by scene end), far from the manuscript card beside the author on the left. The author faces the viewer with his hands down and does not look or gesture at the manuscript. The visual says 'inspect the people', not 'begin with the edited manuscript'.
defects.fix: Put the magnifier over the manuscript card, or in the author's hand aimed at it, with the author's gaze on the card and an inviting hand toward it. Optionally, let the '?' on the card link to the uncovered conflict.

defects.what: The specialists do not 'tend a necessary part'. The planner's clipboard floats in mid-air beside her head (not held) and the gauge hangs almost touching her hair, so props crowd her silhouette. Both stand facing the viewer with their hands at their sides and do not look at the gauge or the valve. The engineer (orange) is far below the valve, and her V-shaped brows read as anger, not 'thoughtful concern'.
defects.fix: Have the planner hold the clipboard and look up at the gauge, with clear space between the gauge and her head. Have the engineer reach up to or turn the valve with concerned (not angry) brows. Both should face their own section, away from the leaking joint behind them.

defects.what: 'The author remains uncertain, but keeps asking…': the author enters at the far right edge, crowded about 10 px behind the engineer, faces the viewer with a broad smile and his arms down, and does not look or gesture at the red question circle or the leak. The broad smile contradicts 'remains uncertain', and no asking is embodied.
defects.fix: Bring the author toward the centre near the leak/question (not behind the engineer). Use a thoughtful, slightly uncertain expression (cautious hope at most a small smile), raise his hand in a question gesture and turn his gaze to the leak, holding this through the sentence midpoint.

defects.what: The author stands detached at the far left, about 90 px from the desk, facing the viewer in every midpoint frame, and never looks at the drafts or the laptop. The laptop screen is blank. The cue 'sharp original sentence become smoother while its question fades' is only half shown: the Original card keeps full-strength red throughout, and only the Smoothed card gains a faint zig-zag ghost.
defects.fix: Seat or stand the author at the desk, looking up at the cards during sentence 1 (disappointed), and dim/desaturate the original question as the smoothed version appears. In sentence 2, turn his gaze/invite gesture to the book cover.

defects.what: In sentence 1 the red '?' floats outside the passage card's left edge and the author does not look at the passage. In sentence 2/last, the three connector lines meet in empty space between the router's antennas instead of attaching to the router, and they start about 20 px below the icons. In Night, the red '?' is low-contrast on black.
defects.fix: Anchor the '?' inside the card margin or at the author's raised hand. End the connectors on the router body. Brighten the Night '?' colour.

defects.what: The resident (grey hair, red coat) has an unexplained white horizontal bar across her chest/scarf at collar height (apparently the mirrored V-collar flattened into a rectangle), plus a stray thin peach line across her hair above the glasses. Reads as a rendering artifact on a main character in every theme and frame of the scene.
defects.fix: Render the resident's collar as a proper mirrored V-collar (or remove it) and remove the stray forehead/hair stroke; verify the mirrored rig parts at 3x zoom.

defects.what: The author's face for 'engaged clarity' (scene 2, 'The book follows a similar pattern...') and 'determined'/'inviting challenge' (scene 4, 'Begin with the edited manuscript...') is drawn with steep V brows and a flat clenched mouth, which reads as an angry scowl. The narration and emotional plan are calm invitation, so the closing invitation looks hostile.
defects.fix: Use level or slightly raised brows with a small closed smile or soft open mouth for engaged clarity; for inviting challenge use level focused brows and a slight confident smile, with an open palm toward the manuscript.

defects.what: In Night the factory chimney (rgb 59,58,57), the microscope eyepiece cap and stage/arm (rgb 14,32,45) and the microscope base (59,58,57) sit on the near-black stage (6,9,15). The cap and stage are effectively invisible (~1.3:1), so the 'research' microscope loses its shape and the factory loses its chimney.
defects.fix: Give these parts Night-theme tokens with at least ~3:1 contrast against the stage (for example light slate #9fb3c8 for the cap/stage and mid grey #8a8a8a for the chimney/base).

defects.what: The planned 'open defending hand, leaning back' of the operator renders as the same straight horizontal arm ending in a fist as the resident's accusing point. The two mirrored fists meet mid-gap and read as symmetric pointing or a fist bump, not accusation and defence. The operator shows no visible lean back.
defects.fix: Bend the operator's elbow and raise an open palm (fingers visible) at chest height toward the resident, tilt the torso and head back a few degrees, and keep the resident's extended index-finger point. Different arm silhouettes make the conflict legible.

defects.what: On 'a book about systems that miss the damage they cause' the author has a wide open-mouth laughing grin, which is too gleeful for the planned 'clear interest' (intensity 0.35) and clashes with 'damage'. His pointing arm also ends in a fist about 140 px short of the book.
defects.fix: Use a closed or slight smile with raised brows, and an open hand or index point that clearly reaches toward the book cover.

defects.what: The left and right link lines run diagonally through the router's antenna stems before ending on the body, so the lines and antennas form crossed X shapes, which looks tangled. The author's pointing fist also aims at empty space left of the network rather than at the domains or the hub.
defects.fix: Move the antennas to the outer ends of the router body, or end the diagonal links inside the antennas so no line crosses an antenna. Aim the author's open hand toward the hub or the three domains.

defects.frames: qa/screenshots/*-03-sentence-1.png; *-03-first.png and *-03-last.png show the empty upper half
defects.what: The 'All systems align.' card floats in empty space above the pair and never softens or partially masks the conflict, so 'harder to notice' is only stated, not shown. Outside sentence 1 the upper half of the stage is empty, leaving the composition bottom-heavy.
defects.fix: Without crossing faces, let the card descend so its lower edge partly covers the pair's raised arms or the gap between them, so the disagreement is half-hidden. Then lift it away in sentence 2. Alternatively, dim the pair under it slightly.

defects.what: Author's raised hand toward the drip/question is a fingerless round ball (no palm or index finger), and his face keeps the same worried frown as both specialists; the plan's 'cautious hope' for 'keeps asking where people can still make a useful difference' has no visible cue.

defects.what: The 'All systems align.' card's lower corners clip the operator's raised hand (only thumb and finger stubs poke out beside the corner) and swallow the resident's forearm, so the pointing anger gesture is invisible while 'real conflict' is spoken; it reads as a z-order/cropping glitch or as the pair jointly holding a banner, and a text label overlaps character silhouettes.

defects.what: Once the card lifts, the operator's raised open palm with spread fingers sits at shoulder/head height facing out and reads as a friendly wave/hello rather than a defensive 'hold on' (PRODUCTION.md claims chest height); with the resident pointing into empty space ~170 px away the confrontation reads as a greeting.
defects.fix: Lower the palm to chest height, fingers together, angled toward the resident's finger, and make the backward lean visible.
